messages:
maya: FYI CI flagged a weird rendering in the gpu-worker chart — nodeSelector ended up as a quoted string which the cluster-autoscaler ignored, so we spun up extra nodes. Pipeline: https://ci.internal/redwood/12345 :grimacing:
infra-ci: helm template failed: templates/worker/deployment.yaml: error converting YAML to JSON: yaml: line 42: did not find expected mapping key
devon: can you paste the rendered snippet or the helper? my hunch: the helper that emits nodeSelector is returning a YAML list/string instead of a map, so k8s sees a scalar where it expects map[string]string
maya: rendered snippet from the job:
```
# -- rendered fragment --
nodeSelector: "{\"nodepool\":\"p4-v2\"}"
# -- end --
```
devon: ahh — that exact symptom happens when someone does `toYaml (list (dict \"nodepool\" .Values.gpu.pool))` vs just `toYaml (dict \"nodepool\" .Values.gpu.pool)`. toYaml on a stringified JSON can also produce quotes.
ankit: the helper in question (templates/_helpers.tpl) currently has:
```
{{- define \"infra.gpuSelector\" -}}
{{- if and .Values.gpu.enabled .Values.gpu.pool -}}
nodeSelector: {{ toYaml (list (dict \"nodepool\" .Values.gpu.pool)) | nindent 8 }}
{{- end -}}
{{- end -}}
```
ankit: using `list` wraps the dict in a YAML sequence, and in some chart consumers we then patch/merge that into other maps which ends up stringifying the whole block. also our values.schema.json doesn't validate shapes for `gpu` so bad types slip in.
devon: suggested quick fix: change helper to emit a plain map, and be explicit about types in values.schema.json. e.g.
```
{{- define \"infra.gpuSelector\" -}}
{{- if and .Values.gpu.enabled .Values.gpu.pool -}}
nodeSelector:
  nodepool: "{{ .Values.gpu.pool }}"
{{- end -}}
{{- end -}}
```
or use `toYaml (dict \"nodepool\" .Values.gpu.pool) | nindent 8` (no list).
maya: opened a patch: https://git.internal/redwood/charts/pulls/549 — includes helper fix + values.schema.json change to require `gpu.pool` as string and `gpu.enabled` boolean. I also added a unit test for `helm template` to catch quoted scalars.
infra-ci: PR 549 lint results: templates/worker/deployment.yaml -> ok, values.schema.json -> ok, helm unittest -> failed on one case (overlay with empty map)
devon: the failing overlay case happens when an overlay sets `gpu: {}` (empty map) — our helper `and .Values.gpu.enabled .Values.gpu.pool` treats missing keys as nil, but when overlays exist they can coerce types. We should defensively coerce: `and (hasKey .Values \"gpu\") (eq .Values.gpu.enabled true) (and (hasKey .Values.gpu \"pool\") (ne .Values.gpu.pool \"\"))` — bit verbose but avoids false positives.
ankit: alternative: use `required` in values.schema for `gpu.pool` when `gpu.enabled` is true via `oneOf`/`if`/`then` pattern in JSON schema. that will make CI fail earlier.
sre-lead: thanks team — hold the deploy for this chart until PR 549 merges and we run a quick canary in staging. schedule a short postmortem on Monday to cover how patch/merge semantics with overlay maps caused this. :+1:
maya: will do. added a short runbook note in the PR about how quoted nodeSelector breaks autoscaler health checks and increases cost (observed ~2x scale for that run). I'll follow up with a small alert to watch for similar patterns in other charts.
devon: nice catch — also adding a lint rule to detect `toYaml` -> quoted scalar patterns is doable. can do a follow-up PR.
ankit: I ran a quick grep — 4 charts use `toYaml (list (dict` — filing issues for each.
infra-ci: deploy blocked by PR 549 until manual approval.
